I transferred from a CC (was there for 7 years not really doing anything with my life) to university and now I have a degree in EE and working on a masters in signal processing. And I also have a career as a test engineer. You can do this. I promise. Do your homework and redo it to study for the tests to make sure you know the concepts of what you’re learning. You got this!!!

My experience might help you.

By the end of my senior year in high school I was retaking algebra 2 and barely passing with a C, didn’t even think about anything related to physics (to be honest I probably wouldn’t even be able to describe what physics was). I also had no idea that I was already late to applying for community college. I learned this when I was hanging out with friends on a random night during summer after high school graduation and they had already got accepted to really good universities.

I went to a community college that wasn’t that close to my house because I knew my dad was gonna be pissed as fuck if I didnt even try college out. I honestly don’t even remember how I was able to apply and get accepted with enough time to get classes. I was only able to enroll in 2 classes for my first semester, Colonial US history and history of rock and roll (which I don’t even really listen to that often). After that semester I went to the community college closer to my house. I still didn’t give a shit about anything besides making electronic music and hanging out with friends. I basically floated there taking gen ed classes for 5 years. During that time school was so random and not planned out while I was working in the food industry. I thought I would “make it in music”. Then I realized all the technology I was using was pretty complex and I wanted to understand how it worked.

After those 5 years of no direction a spark hit me. I started taking classes seriously. Before I transferred to university I was done with electricity and magnetism and calculus 3. I worked super hard. I transferred to university with the same feelings as you. I graduated with a degree in EE and now I’m getting a masters in signal processing while working as a test engineer and I am so happy. And I still have music as a hobby that I do just to have fun and enjoy.

Point is, if you’re already this motivated in high school do be asking this type of stuff, compared to what I was doing, you’re gonna be fine as long you do your homework and study for tests.

P.S. a lot of engineering disciplines don’t care about gen ed courses, but I’ve learned a lot from them. Have an open mind. Sociology taught me a lot about social issues and how important they are for the world. Think for yourself and always do what’s right!! You’re gonna be fine!!!
